reviews.title: Defective text-to-speech
reviews.text:
When using Read Aloud with a seemingly stable high speed internet connection, Edge will intermittently display the message "switched to offline voice due to poor internet connection" and then continue to read the page using a (vastly inferior) offline voice. When this occurs there is no evidence of an internet service disruption and the problem has been observed while using various ISPs. Moreover, once the switch to offline voice has transpired, Edge will remain stuck in that mode for a particular tab until Edge is restarted. Note that this is specific to a particular tab—if one tab has switched to offline voice mode, Read Aloud can be started in another tab and will use the normal high quality online voice for that other tab. This bug first manifested with the upgrade to version 139.

This is a very unfortunate bug in that it significantly degrades the user experience especially of the visually impaired. When functioning normally, Edge’s text-to-speech functionality was the best on the market and a real boon for users who by choice or necessity consumed audio renditions of text. I assume that Microsoft has has diverted significant resources to promoting Copilot (to the detriment of other features), but it would be a great service if Microsoft would spare the personnel to attend to this bug promptly.
